records.name: DynaMate (Mendible-Barreto et al.)
records.demonstrated_target: liquid water, alanine dipeptide in vacuum, and IRMOF-1/ethanol system construction
records.boundary_conditions: water simulation cell; alanine dipeptide explicitly in vacuum; IRMOF-1 framework and ethanol preparation shown separately

sources.locator: Worked examples Figs.5–9 and Figs.12–13; full original manuscript also read at the ResearchGate mirror
sources.evidence_paraphrase: LLM agents call Moltemplate/Packmol tools to construct IRMOF-1 plus ethanol, prepare water minimization/NPT/NVT input, and launch a stable five-nanosecond LAMMPS run. Alanine-dipeptide metadynamics produces sampled dihedrals and a reconstructed free-energy surface.

sources.locator: Original RSC full manuscript, especially Figs.7,9,12,13
sources.evidence_paraphrase: The complete primary manuscript is readable here despite publisher HTTP403. It identifies template-based tool selection and notes that some generated inputs still require human editing.

sources.locator: README; tutorials/1_system_prep; tutorials/2_sim_runner; tutorials/4_enhanced_sampler
sources.evidence_paraphrase: Author repository supplies the corresponding LAMMPS/Moltemplate tools, MOF/solvent preparation files and enhanced-sampling notebooks.

aliases: DynaMate: leveraging AI-agents for customized research workflows
records.limitations: Distinct from Guilbert's protein–ligand DynaMate. Attribution to de Gillis in an earlier discovery lead was incorrect: this paper is by Mendible-Barreto, Díaz-Maldonado, Carmona Esteva, Torres, Córdova-Figueroa and Colón. Cross-domain reflects the actually illustrated framework/solvent construction plus molecular-liquid/dipeptide cases; it does not establish a completed MOF adsorption campaign. MD free-energy sampling is D, not F or R. Template-guided and human-assisted.

records.name: ChatMat
records.demonstrated_target: ammonia tetramer and water-octamer energy/force comparison; additional water and perchloric-acid ensembles
records.boundary_conditions: explicit worked DFT comparison is finite molecular clusters; PWDFT plane waves do not alone establish an extended-material target

sources.locator: Original accepted manuscript §§2.2–2.4; Figs.4 and7; Fig.7 execution trace
sources.evidence_paraphrase: A Manager coordinates Computing Designer, DFT Operator, ML Performer and Property Depositor. In Fig.7 the agent obtains the ammonia-tetramer structure, checks for an applicable learned model, falls through to first-principles calculation, and returns its energy/forces for comparison with a retrieved water-octamer result.

sources.locator: Journal publication; accepted manuscript dated23April2026
sources.evidence_paraphrase: The paper explicitly extends the earlier MatAgent DFT-operator architecture into a separately evaluated multi-agent framework.

sources.locator: Archived ChatMat v1.1; publication date2February2026
sources.evidence_paraphrase: The author release archives the code and evaluation data before the inspected journal date.

sources.locator: README; evl_results/run1/experiment_results_T1.jsonl through T3.jsonl
sources.evidence_paraphrase: Official implementation and recorded evaluation responses were read. These support the system identity, but response text alone is not treated as an independent numerical validation.

aliases: ChatMat: a multi-agent chemist for autonomous material prediction and exploration
records.limitations: Counted separately from earlier MatAgent because the architecture and evaluation are separately described; retain shared family for sensitivity. The concrete cluster DFT trace determines target classification. Alloy structure acquisition and model-training claims do not establish a separately simulated periodic alloy here. General AIMD equations are not credited as a demonstrated D task. Date is the earliest inspected archived release, not a verified original project launch.

records.name: CatGo
records.demonstrated_target: Pt(111) ORR adsorbates and references; multi-facet Ni catalysis including CO dissociation; ORCA molecular reaction and UV–Vis workflows
records.boundary_conditions: periodic Pt/Ni slabs with vacuum; separate molecular ORCA workflows; interface trajectories are distinguished from isolated species

sources.locator: Full original RSC manuscript §§2.3,5–7; Fig.4; Table6; §7.6–7.7 references SI S3.6 andS6
sources.evidence_paraphrase: CLI agents assemble the same editable DAG used by the UI. The executed Pt ORR graph connects slab/adsorbate construction, VASP optimization, frequencies and free-energy analysis, with DOS/COHP outputs. A 26-node MACE Ni reproduction reports CO-dissociation barriers. The paper identifies executed molecular ORCA reaction/TDDFT counterparts in SI S6.

sources.locator: Published article identity
sources.evidence_paraphrase: Journal version of the same CatGo project; it is not counted separately from its ChemRxiv report.

sources.locator: Archived release25July2026; SI_pt111_orr_workflow.json; mace_ni_smoke.workflow.json; Reaction_Workflow.json; UV-Vis.json
sources.evidence_paraphrase: Author archive supplies the executable graphs. The molecular graph has optimization, TS search, frequency and IRC nodes; a separate azo-molecule graph has optimization and TDDFT. Graph definitions support reproducibility but are not alone proof of convergence.

sources.locator: Preprint identity/date; direct full-text access unavailable
sources.evidence_paraphrase: Earliest located preprint corresponds to this same system, dated11May2026; the scientific coding uses the inspected published manuscript.

records.limitations: High architectural relevance to Cloudra: shared visual/agent DAG, explicit dependencies, backend execution and results. Scientific choices remain human controlled. R is supported by the reported Ni CO-dissociation reproduction; the ORR free-energy diagram alone would not support it. D is deliberately unmarked because demonstrated trajectory analysis and implemented MD support were not independently traced to agent-launched dynamics in the inspected examples. Molecular and surface execution is explicitly stated in the original paper; full SI numerical tables were not retrieved. Earliest date is a located preprint date, with direct DOI metadata access limited.

records.name: El Agente Potente
records.demonstrated_target: bulk crystals and Li-ion conductors; tetraethylene glycol dibenzoate conformers; alanine-dipeptide metadynamics; HKUST-1 adsorption; Fe-surface reactions
records.boundary_conditions: periodic bulk/slab/MOF calculations and explicitly isolated molecular conformers; molecular enhanced sampling separately identified

sources.locator: §§2.1–2.3; Figs.2–5; supplementary Molecular/Adsorption/Catalytic Case Studies and agent traces
sources.evidence_paraphrase: Typed execution graphs and a complementary coding agent run actual MLIP workflows. Examples include crystal relaxation/phonons, generated Li-conductor MD, isolated-molecule conformer sampling with ten PySCF single points and frequencies, alanine metadynamics, adsorption, and seven-image Fe(110) NEB plus Sella refinement with two MACE potentials.

records.limitations: Distinct named architecture after the earlier six El Agente workflows; shared family must be used in a family-merged sensitivity analysis. Some molecular DFT steps are coordinated through El Agente Gráfico rather than a newly invented backend. MD transport and GCMC results are screening-level; substantial MLIP dependence remains. Task coverage is not a claim of correct mechanisms or autonomous scientific acceptance. GCMC is not recoded as MD; D is independently established by real MD/metadynamics cases.

records.name: Agent-E2MD
records.demonstrated_target: Ar, Ag, Bi, Si, Ni and Al benchmarks; graphene with water, carbon dioxide and ammonia reactive adsorbates
records.boundary_conditions: periodic bulk benchmarks; three-dimensionally periodic graphene/C–H–O–N test cell

sources.locator: §§2.5–2.6; §§3–4; Methods7.5, especially zero-temperature and finite-temperature benchmark protocols
sources.evidence_paraphrase: LLM agents translate interaction equations into compiled LAMMPS pair styles, repair build/runtime failures, launch single-point, lattice/defect/elastic and MD validation, then compare numerical results with references. Seven potential/material pairs include finite-temperature metals/Si and a reactive graphene-plus-adsorbates trajectory.

records.limitations: Included as simulation-software development with actual atomistic execution and feedback, consistent with the baseline admitting algorithm-improvement workflows. It is not an autonomous catalyst-discovery agent. Structure setup is a fixed benchmark initializer, so no extra T mark; reactive dynamics and evolving bond order do not establish an explicit TS/path search R. Adsorbate molecules on graphene do not create a separate molecular-target category.

records.name: GBClaw
records.demonstrated_target: 14 asymmetric tilt grain boundaries in nickel; reconstruction and shear-coupled migration
records.boundary_conditions: Ni bicrystals with periodic boundary conditions within the grain-boundary plane and upper/lower free surfaces; compact supercells explicitly limit long-range defects

sources.locator: Original51-page PDF; main pp.4–8, Fig.5 and pp.16–18; Methods pp.21–24; Supplementary Notes4–7
sources.evidence_paraphrase: A planning/structure/LAMMPS/analysis agent team constructs and relaxes Ni bicrystals, calculates grain-boundary energies and athermal shear response. Human-guided replanning triggers loading/unloading and a 144-replica NEB connecting the initial and reconstructed boundary states.

sources.locator: Official demonstration linked by the original manuscript
sources.evidence_paraphrase: Author demonstration is a reproducibility pointer; task marks here derive from the original paper rather than an uninspected video.

records.limitations: R is a solid-state reconstruction minimum-energy path, not an organic reaction TS. The reported shear calculations are athermal displacement/minimization sequences; the paper places large-scale finite-temperature MD in future work, so D remains unmarked. Human-guided mechanistic interpretation and compact-cell limitations are explicit. Original PDF downloaded/read because arXiv HTML was unavailable and web PDF exceeded the size limit.

records.name: MDAgent2-RUNTIME
records.demonstrated_target: LAMMPS materials simulations; Cu–Ni nanoparticle melting worked trajectory
records.boundary_conditions: finite Cu–Ni nanoparticle is the concrete worked target; box periodicity not independently reconstructed

sources.locator: §2.4; Methods3.3 Runtime Multi-Agent Framework; Appendix8 Case Study
sources.evidence_paraphrase: A deployable generator/runner/evaluator loop writes LAMMPS input, checks potential availability, executes scripts, evaluates results and revises failures. The worked Cu–Ni melting trace repairs an unavailable EAM filename, runs LAMMPS and re-enters generation after a low evaluation score.

sources.locator: Official code URL identified in the original paper
sources.evidence_paraphrase: Project identity and implementation pointer for MDAgent2 rather than an unrelated biomolecular MDAgent.

records.limitations: Separately described runtime/training architecture builds on the2025 MDAgent; count separately under the dataset's architecture-level rule and combine for family sensitivity. MD-GRPO and MD-EvalBench are components, not additional agents. The illustrative appendix omits code/output details and contains placeholders; task coverage also rests on the execution benchmark, and no scientific success rate or extra T/E/O tasks are inferred.

records.name: PVmatAgent
records.demonstrated_target: Cs2AgBiBr6→Cs2AgBiCl6 substitution and inorganic/hybrid perovskite screening
records.boundary_conditions: periodic crystallographic CIF models; organic cations in hybrid crystals do not imply isolated molecular targets

sources.locator: Methods2.1–2.2; Results3.1 Case1, especially elemental substitution followed by CHGNet relaxation and formation-energy evaluation
sources.evidence_paraphrase: The LLM retrieves Cs2AgBiBr6, invokes a Br→Cl structure-editing tool and immediately calls CHGNet to relax the new crystal. The case reports formation-energy evaluation before the separate scalar bandgap/device models are used.

sources.locator: README; expert-tool matrix; typical scientific showcases
sources.evidence_paraphrase: Official repository identifies the LLM tool-dispatch architecture and CHGNet structure/energy tools. VASP scheduling support alone is not treated as an executed DFT case.

sources.locator: Earlier preprint identity, May2026 lead; precise primary posting date unresolved
sources.evidence_paraphrase: Same authors and system, with a slightly different title; retained as a version alias rather than a second system.

aliases: Photovoltaic Materials Mixture of Experts Agent
records.limitations: Date uses the inspected journal first-publication date; an earlier May2026 ChemRxiv version and an April repository exist, so this is not a verified earliest appearance. Inclusion rests on actual force-field relaxation, not GNN bandgap prediction or device-level efficiency modeling. No completed VASP calculation was established. Source explicitly warns of representation/model errors in hybrid perovskites; coverage does not validate the quantitative physical claims. Publisher main text was readable through its indexed full original page while some direct opens returned403.

records.boundary_conditions: periodic plane-wave crystals/slabs with explicit vacuum detection; no cross-domain claim from a preparatory H2 check

sources.evidence_paraphrase: Kimi/Claude-compatible MCP tools let an LLM construct/fetch a MoS2 model, relax it with GPAW and calculate bands/DOS. The official worked demonstrations link machine-readable convergence/results and a separate QE comparison.

sources.locator: E0–E8; E1 agent-generated incorrect interpretation of an actually executed MoS2 workflow; later dated cases

It also records failed LiCoO2 and parameter trials rather than hiding them.

sources.locator: relaxed.cif; convergence.json; summary.json; workflow_result.json
sources.evidence_paraphrase: Official run artifacts separately expose the relaxed geometry, convergence tests and final electronic output. These provide concrete simulation evidence beyond an installed tool list.

records.limitations: Developer project demonstration, without a located independent original research paper or benchmark. Include under the same official-demonstration sensitivity used for Protomia/Chelatron. First date is the dated developer case record and repository creation date, not a reviewed publication. Some early bulk relaxations are near-equilibrium validation rather than an extensive structural search. Numerical agreement against Materials Project PBE is implementation consistency, not experimental accuracy.

records.name: DynaMate2
records.demonstrated_target: aqueous NaCl:267water molecules and one Na+/Cl− pair
records.boundary_conditions: explicit periodic20Å cubic solution box; molecular liquid remains soft matter

sources.locator: Introduction pp.2–3; §4 Representative Example pp.10–14; Table2 and Fig.4
sources.evidence_paraphrase: A persistent LangGraph supervisor/specialist hierarchy coordinates registered expert tools. The actual single-instruction case downloads MACE-POLAR, converts molecular SMILES, packs267waters plus NaCl, runs250ps ASE NVT dynamics and plots trajectory energy/temperature. The authors explicitly contrast this architecture with the first DynaMate single-tool-per-prompt design.

sources.locator: Primary version history
sources.evidence_paraphrase: First submitted20May2026;9June2026revision is the same DynaMate2 system, not another count.

aliases: DynaMate2: runtime registration of expert-defined tools for agentic scientific workflow automation
records.limitations: Separate from DynaMate under the baseline architecture/workflow unit: genuine supervisor coordination, persistent runtime tool registration and a new end-to-end MLIP demonstration. Combine with its predecessor for family sensitivity. The illustrated run tests orchestration, not NaCl thermodynamics or MLIP accuracy. No extra E for trajectory energies or O for unreported minimization. Currentv2 places a code-review critic in future work; do not describe it as implemented.

screening.name: ISAAC / agentic XPS framework (Shen and Qian)
screening.locator: Original abstract; author group page https://qiangrouppage.lbl.gov/research
screening.reason: The original abstract now explicitly identifies an end-to-end demonstration on eleven gas-phase reaction intermediates with C1s/O1s ΔSCF energies, including radicals and an iodine species. Thus VASP support must not cause automatic materials/cross-domain classification; demonstrated target appears finite molecules. Direct full report remained inaccessible and author code was not located, so the individual execution/relaxation traces remain unverified. Preserve as a highly probable eligible system pending full-text audit, not an absence-of-capability claim.

sources.locator: Original preprint abstract, no full file available
sources.evidence_paraphrase: Reports an LLM supervisor with human approvals and an actual eleven-species gas-phase XPS demonstration; no full calculation trace was available here.

screening.name: MatBrain
screening.reason: Read the official released Figure5 conversation transcript at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MAIC-SIAT/matbrain/main/figure-data/figure5/matbrain_session_20260525_105145.md. It shows failed fractional-formula queries, then database lookup and CrystaLLM generation of a mixed-halide perovskite; no MatGL relaxation tool is called in this complete trace. Earlier SI-listed relaxation tools still do not establish execution. The main article is paywalled and arXiv:2604.11540 HTML unavailable; no negative claim about uninspected catalyst screening is made.

screening.name: DFT AutoPilot
screening.reason: Official README was read. It supplies QE/VASP/Gaussian orchestration and a typical Si session with numerical results, but that dialogue is illustrative and no dated retained run artifacts were located in this pass. It is a useful tool lead, not another main entry solely from installed capability or example prompts.
